description: Design the Caledonian crow gripper for the SO-101 arms. Jake asked for this to exist as a pebble and for Vigil to start here once it does. The name points at the New Caledonian crow, which makes and uses hooked tools — so the idea is a hook-led end effector rather than a parallel jaw: fewer actuated parts, grip by shape and leverage instead of pinch force. Work out what that actually means for the SO-101's wrist mount and payload before designing anything, and say what you decided and why. Two existing plans in the queue are the surrounding context and should be read first: voice-3c221288 (a collapsible humanoid rig mounting two SO-101 arms) and voice-c7737295 (which open model to run on those arms). The north star is the MolmoAct2 VLA video (voice-4858e8fa) — zero-shot manipulation rather than hand-built task logic — so a gripper that only works with bespoke scripted motions is the wrong answer. This repo has a CAD loop at Scripts/cadloop for iterating on geometry by voice; use it rather than building a second one.

results.identified_issue:
REQUEST: design the Caledonian crow gripper for the SO-101 as a HOOK-LED end effector (fewer actuated parts, grip by shape and leverage rather than pinch force). Explicitly: work out what that means for the wrist mount and payload BEFORE designing anything, and say what was decided and why. Use Scripts/cadloop rather than building a second loop. North star is voice-4858e8fa (MolmoAct2 zero-shot VLA) — a gripper that only works with bespoke scripted motion is the wrong answer.

CONTEXT THIS BUILDS ON. voice-15d564c5 already shipped cad/openscad/crow/ — a NC-crow-beak jaw pair on the unmodified SO-101 mount. That is a forceps, not a hook. This item is the next question, not a repeat, so I did not touch that geometry.

THE PREMISE CORRECTION, and it is load-bearing. The brief reasons "NC crow makes hooked tools, therefore hooked end effector". The NC crow's BILL is not hooked — it is notably less decurved than other corvids (the previous agent got this right and deliberately left the hook off). The hooks are on the manufactured tools. So the bird licenses two different projects: a hooked gripper, or a gripper that CHUCKS a hook. I kept the principle (load carried by shape) and rejected the literal claw, and named the tool-chuck reading as the better long game since crow_opening_for_rod() already half-implements it.

WHY NOT 0 DoF, which is the obvious reading of "fewer actuated parts". The SO-101 gripper is ALREADY one actuator and one DoF — there is nothing to remove except the actuator itself. A passive hook fails the north star twice: (a) the policy's gripper channel would command nothing, and (b) getting a load into and out of a passive hook requires a specific approach-hook-lift-tilt trajectory, i.e. exactly the bespoke scripted motion the brief forbids. Dropping to zero actuators does not simplify the robot, it moves the mechanism into the policy where we cannot train it. So the hook cannot pay in part count; it has to pay in force and holding.

THE NUMBERS, all derived in-repo, not recalled:
- Lever arms from the pivot (4.4, 23.375): fingertip 83.78 mm (crow_tip_arm, echoed on compile), tool notch 56.69 mm (crow_notch_r), commissure hypot(-12.4-4.4, 62-23.375) = 42.1 mm. So 1.48x and 1.99x the tip force at the same servo torque.
- Mass, by a volume integral over the committed STL exports (scratch script, stdlib struct): stock fixed 66.36 cm^3 + moving 21.74 = 88.10; crow upper 66.04 + lower 21.02 = 87.05. 1.2% lighter, same z=105.375 tip. The beak swap is mass- and moment-neutral — that is the baseline a hook must match.
- Wrist moment: 0.5 kg at the fingertip is 0.52 N.m at 105.4 mm. Holding at the notch is 27.4 mm closer (26% off the effector's share), at the commissure 43.4 mm (41%).
- Grip force a friction pinch needs: 0.5 kg / 2 mu at mu~0.4 is ~6 N sustained, against a position-controlled servo with no force sensing — which hand_1_0.md already calls the least certain thing in the design.

THE STRONGEST PRO-HOOK ARGUMENT IS NOT THE BIRD. MolmoAct2's observation space is RGB + joint positions with NO force or tactile channel (plans/molmoact2.md). A model that cannot sense force cannot regulate it, so holding that comes from geometry is strictly easier to drive than holding that comes from a commanded squeeze. That is a better argument than the crow analogy and it is what I built section 5 on.

THE RESIDUAL RISK I did not resolve: the SO100/101 checkpoint's community training data was recorded with the stock stepped jaws in frame, so ANY reshaped effector is an embodiment shift in the wrist camera's view. Unknowable until there is a camera and a baseline number, hence D7 (don't print until then), which is molmoact2.md's cheapest-test-first applied unchanged.

DECISIONS: D1 arm interface frozen. D2 keep one actuator and open/close semantics; the servo's job changes from "squeeze hard enough" to "shut the gate". D3 the hook is a gated throat between the mandibles, not a barb on one — a claw snags when open, which is a liability under a brittle policy. D4 throat at z 62-78, not the tip. D5 tip stays at 105.375 and stays a working forceps; the hook is a second grip mode at the root. D6 keep the V notch (the hooked-TOOL reading). D7 don't print yet. REJECTED: passive 0-DoF hook, a second servo for a latch, a claw past the fingertip, any change to the mount.

CADLOOP. It was hardwired to cad/openscad/params.scad + gripper.scad and could not see the crow tree at all. Added a TARGETS table (dir/params/main/geom) selected by CADLOOP_TARGET, defaulting to gripper so nothing about the existing loop changes. Verified: bogus target and missing-file guards both exit 2 (which also proves the module parses, since ESM parses fully before executing); a crow render with the loop's own camera and fast_preview args is 0.23 s; the stock model still reports 73 live / 7 dead with the identical dead names.

THE BUG WIRING IT EXPOSED, and this is the part a future agent should know. params.mjs computed liveness as "does a geometry file name this parameter". On the stock gripper every station table is named directly by moving_jaw.scad so it never showed. On the beak, crow_tomium / crow_culmen / crow_gonys / crow_lower_tomium / crow_width — the lists that ARE the shape — are read only through crow_tomium_x() and siblings defined inside crow_params.scad, so they scored "indirect" and the SYS prompt never offered them. The loop would have rendered the beak and silently refused to reshape it, which is the same class of failure params.mjs was written to prevent. Liveness now also follows the params file's own `function` definitions, transitively (reachedFunctions()). Functions only, not modules — a module in a params file emits geometry and there are none in either model. INVARIANT I CHECKED: the stock model's dead list is still exactly the same seven names, because those are the documented traps the refusal messages are written against. One stock name moved indirect -> live (jaw_tip_arm); it is an expression, and setScalar's regex only matches a bare number, so an attempted edit fails cleanly with "did not change" rather than corrupting the file.

GRAMMAR: added beak/bill/mandible/gape/commissure to SUBJECTS and made the opening lever resolve jaw_opening OR crow_opening from a two-name list, so "open the beak 10 millimetres" stays in the 1 ms deterministic lane instead of paying the model's 1.5 s. Every other lever is hardcoded to mj_*/fj_* names and returns null on the crow model (num() returns null and each lever guards), so it degrades to the model lane cleanly rather than erroring.

IF THIS IS WRONG, in order of likelihood. (a) Jake may want the literal hooked claw and may not care that the bird does not have one — D4 is the thing to react to and the fix is to move the throat out to the tip, at a known cost of 2x the force and 41% more wrist moment. (b) jaw_pivot_x / jaw_pivot_z are the one inferred pair in the whole model (NOTES.md section 6) and EVERY lever arm above rests on them; calipers settle it in a minute. (c) The 0.5 kg / 413 mm figures are inherited from voice-3c221288, not measured — every percentage I quote is a ratio and survives a correction, the absolute headroom does not. (d) NOT YET SOLVED and a prerequisite before any throat is cut: crow_params.scad's closed-form interference proof assumes radius-from-pivot climbs monotonically along the tomium, and a throat is a local DIP in that radius, so it WILL trip that assert. The proof has to be extended to a piecewise-monotonic tomium first. (e) Nothing printed, no load, no sheet of paper.
results.summary: Worked out what hook-led costs at the wrist and decided the hook goes at the back of the beak, not the front — written up in plans/crow_gripper.md, no geometry cut yet.
results.detailed_description:
One correction first, because it changes the design: the New Caledonian crow's bill is not hooked. It is conspicuously straighter than other crows — the hooks are on the sticks it makes. So I read "hook-led" as load carried by shape instead of by pinch force, which is a mechanical property rather than a silhouette.

Two things the wrist decides for us. There is one actuator and one gripper.pos channel, so "fewer actuated parts" has nowhere to go but zero — and a passive hook has no "close" for a VLA to command and needs a scripted approach to load it, which is the thing the MolmoAct2 north star rules out. And I measured the jaws off the committed STLs: 87.05 cm³ for the beak against 88.10 for the stock pair, same 105.4 mm tip, so the swap is already payload-neutral. What actually matters is where the load hangs. Holding at the commissure instead of the fingertip is 1.99× the grip force from the same servo torque and 41% less wrist moment. Both constraints point the same way, and that is the decision: keep the servo, keep the mount untouched, and make the hook a gated throat at z 62–78 rather than a claw past the tip.

I also pointed Scripts/cadloop at the beak — it was hardwired to the stock gripper and could not see it. Run it with CADLOOP_TARGET=crow. Doing that turned up a real bug: the loop scored a parameter "live" only if a geometry file named it directly, so the three lists that ARE the beak's shape were invisible to the edit engine and it would have rendered the beak then refused to reshape it.

Read section 6 of plans/crow_gripper.md and react to D4 — the hook at the back of the beak rather than the front. Everything else follows from it, and I'll cut the throat geometry in the loop once you say. Nothing here has touched hardware, and the 0.5 kg payload figure is inherited from the rig plan, not measured.
